decisions.reason: A reference class electrometer is core dosimetry measurement technology in which the firm holds deep related knowledge, and its home page placement in both years shows it is a flagship product the firm can interpret and improve.

Oncology risk management software sits further from the firm's hardware measurement base, but it complements its radiotherapy quality assurance knowledge and has kept a dedicated page for two years, so the firm can likely assimilate the learning it generates.
A CT image quality phantom builds directly on the firm's existing imaging quality assurance and physics expertise, so it is easy to learn from and refine.
The mammography image quality phantom is closely related to the firm's established test-device know-how and to regulatory QA demand, which supports retaining it.
The full field mammography phantom extends the same knowledge base as Product D, but it overlaps with that product, so there is some modest risk of consolidation.

Medical imaging QA instruments are a natural extension of the firm's core measurement competence and its cooperation with research institutions, so it is well positioned to absorb feedback and improve them.
